stages.title: Current account policy and global imbalances
stages.sub: How a country can fix a structural deficit, and why deficits and surpluses persisting worldwide actually matters.

steps.q: A country's firms have low productivity and export goods that cost more to make than rivals' goods. Is this a one-off blip or something that keeps dragging on the current account year after year?
steps.right: Something that keeps dragging on it
steps.wrong: A one-off blip that soon passes
steps.hint: Low productivity does not fix itself overnight.

steps.q: If domestic firms are just less efficient than foreign rivals, will simply changing interest rates or the exchange rate fix that underlying weakness?
steps.right: No, the weakness itself needs to be tackled directly
steps.wrong: Yes, changing rates fixes it fully
steps.hint: Interest rates change spending, but do they make factories more efficient?

steps.q: Training workers, investing in technology and cutting red tape all aim to make firms produce more cheaply and sell more abroad. What kind of policies are these aimed at a current account deficit?
steps.wrong: Policies to cut consumer spending directly
steps.hint: Think about what raises efficiency and lowers costs of production, not just demand.

steps.q: One country runs a large structural deficit while another runs a large structural surplus, and neither shows signs of shrinking. Is this just a short-term wobble, or a lasting feature of the world economy?
steps.right: A lasting feature of the world economy
steps.wrong: Just a short-term wobble that will vanish soon
steps.hint: Both causes you already know are structural, not temporary.

steps.q: A country running a huge deficit is relying on constant borrowing from abroad to pay for it. If lenders suddenly lost confidence and stopped lending, what would happen to that country's currency and financial system?
steps.right: They could come under serious pressure or even crisis
steps.wrong: Nothing, deficits have no effect on lenders' confidence
steps.hint: Borrowing that cannot continue forever creates risk when it stops.
